notes.text: **Signatures are darker and easier to read.** A typed signature is stamped on the signed PDF in blue-black ink with a slight outline, so the script reads clearly on paper. On screen it fills its field in the same ink.
**Drawn signatures** use a thicker, darker pen. The drawing is also cropped to the ink, so it fills the field instead of shrinking.

⌘, and the menu bar's Settings… open Settings → This Mac in the main window: dictation shortcut, microphone, mode, edge glow, meeting reminders, the "Take notes?" offer, open at login, menu bar icon, permissions, Run setup again, dictation history and Disconnect.
Pick which microphone dictation uses, or keep the Mac's default.
The Dictate window's Settings tab is gone; a small version opens only when Hotsauce can't load.
Settings search finds every This Mac setting inside the Mac app.
Clips: screen recordings are sharp on Retina and large screens; small text stays readable, with or without the camera bubble and after a trim.

When you connect an AI tool by signing in, you choose "Everything you can see" or "Team space only, read only". The team-only choice is for a tool many people share, like a team chat's assistant: it reads the team space only and can't change anything.
Settings → Connections marks team-only connections "Team only".
Dictate → Models shows which models hear you and tidy your words, for example "Speech: Deepgram Nova-3 · Offline: Apple, on the Mac · Cleanup: Claude Haiku 5.5".
Pick how your dictations are tidied: Fast (default), Careful (a bigger model, better with names) or Off (your exact words).
Its version now matches the Hotsauce release, and Settings only says Update available when the Mac app itself changed.
Hotsauce.work has a Download the Mac app link that always gets the newest build and shows its version.
Settings has a search box: type "dark mode", "logo" or "backup" and jump straight to that setting. Press / on any Settings page to start typing.
The command menu (⌘K) finds Settings sections too.

**Send a PDF to other people for signature.** On a draft, list who signs (inside or outside your team) and who only gets a copy. Choose whether they sign all at once or one after another, then place each person's fields and press Send.

**Signing links, no account needed.** Each signer gets their own link. It works for 30 days, and only the hash of its secret is kept. The signer opens `/signing/…`, reads the PDF, then signs or declines with a reason.
**Email through Resend** when `RESEND_API_KEY` and `MAIL_FROM` are set. Without them, Send shows each link for the sender to copy.
**Follow progress.** The envelope page shows each person's state: link sent, opened, signed, declined, or waiting for their turn. You can make a new link or email it again.
**When the last person signs,** everyone on the envelope, copies included, gets the sealed PDF and its certificate attached. Both are also saved in Files.

You can move sign-in to another Clerk application (for example from development to production) without anyone losing their clips, conversations, tokens or settings. Everyone signs in once more and carries on. See "Moving sign-in to another Clerk application" in the self-host guide.

Sign: open a PDF in Files and choose Send for signature, place signature, initials, date, text and checkbox fields, then sign by typing or drawing. A sealed signed PDF and an audit certificate are saved in Files next to the original.
Sign is in the left bar.
A task's panel, a note and a file's pop-up each keep their name at the top and × at the top right, with Delete in ⋯ More beside the ×.
A note no longer has a second "Close" button at the bottom.
A file's Rename sits in More with Delete; Download and Share stay beside the preview.
A past Briefcast episode is named in the top bar, not again in the page, and reads at a doc's width.

A clip's transcript is the page's side panel on the right, like a meeting's. It is open when you arrive on a computer, and the Transcript button at the top hides or shows it. On a phone it opens as a sheet, and choosing a line plays from there and closes it.
A saved link, a form, a check-in, a person and a company read at the same width as a doc.
A person's and a company's cards stack in one column: About, Next meeting, Open tasks, then Meetings.
Every item page names the thing once, in the top bar, with its buttons in one order: status, Share, its own buttons, then More.
One status chip: "Personal" or "Team", then "Saved". A board says "Personal" instead of "Private"; a form's Saved is no longer a red button.
Delete and downloads (CSV, Excel, clip download) live in More on every page.
A form's Questions and Answers use the list tabs; its Settings open as a pop-up from a Settings button.
A saved link's Done, Share and Delete move up into the top bar.
Tasks: switch between Inbox, Today, Upcoming, All and Done from tabs above the list, and search the list by name.
Meetings: search your meetings by name or by person from the top of the page.
Every list has the same row at the top: tabs on the left, search on the right.
Forms, Tables, Pages and Check-ins can be searched by name.
Notes, Forms, Tables and Pages have All, Personal and Team tabs.
Files can be searched on a phone.
On a phone, every page's top bar is the same: menu, title, one main button, and More for everything else
On a phone, a doc shows its name at the top instead of its file name
The Ask button no longer covers a board's undo and redo on a phone
The live demo now has Links: saved pages with reading progress, highlights and notes, an arXiv paper with its PDF, a bioRxiv paper, an added PDF and a link an AI tool saved.
Hotsauce.work has a Links card with a short video of it in action.
Sharing looks the same everywhere: a Share button with Copy link inside, in Clips, Forms, Files, Links, Notes and Boards
Boards have a Copy link of their own
Pressing Escape with a menu open closes just the menu
Pages for one thing (a form, a table, a clip, a board, a saved link, a check-in, a person) now show "‹ Forms", "‹ Tables" and so on at the top left to go back to the list.
Every pop-up has an × at its top right.
On a phone, a table's downloads and Delete are behind a "More" button so the table's name has room.
Dictation works with no connection, using speech recognition on your Mac; the pill says "Offline: on-device".
If Hotsauce can't be reached mid-dictation, what you said is written up on your Mac instead of waiting for Retry.
Every app now has its main button in the same place, at the top right: New doc, New note, New form, New table, New check-in, Save a link, Record a voice note.
New form and New table make it straight away and put the cursor in its name, so you type the name on the form or table itself.
On a phone, main buttons show their words instead of only an icon.
A doc's status now reads "Saved" instead of "Committed".

For you: one list of every comment that mentions you, with a count on the rail and a Today tile. Opening an item marks it read; Done takes it off (with Undo); Later brings it back at 9 AM tomorrow or next Monday.
For you in the Go menu.
Settings → Apps shows which Mac app version you have, and whether a newer one is out, with a Download button.
Settings → What's new lists what changed in each release, in plain words.
An "Update available" item in the menu bar menu when a newer Mac app is out.
Links keeps PDFs: save a PDF's address, press Add a PDF, or drop PDFs on Links, and you get a readable copy you can search and highlight, with the PDF itself in Files.
Papers from arXiv, bioRxiv and medRxiv show their authors, date, version, DOI and abstract, and every address of one paper is one link.
Hotsauce opens with no connection, as the last person signed in, with an Offline bar; actions that need the internet are greyed out.
Docs you type in while offline are kept on this device ("Saved on this device") and sent when you're back online, even after a reload.
Text that couldn't be sent (for example, the doc was moved meanwhile) is listed under "Kept on this device" in Docs.
Sign out works offline and takes effect when you reconnect.
On a shared computer, the next person never sees what the last one typed offline, in docs or comments.
The menu in Settings stays in place while you scroll the page.
Links: highlight passages on a saved page and add notes to them. A Highlights tab collects them, and Copy highlights to a Doc turns them into a document.
Every app shows its plain name as its title, and Whiteboard is now called Boards everywhere.
Comment on any team doc, meeting note or task. Type @ and a name to notify a teammate.
Getting started: an admin can choose which doc its last step opens.
Links uses the same screens as the other apps, and buttons use the same words everywhere (New task, New doc, Personal and Team).
A new member's Today starts with a Getting started tile: connect the calendar, get the Mac app, see the docs.
Links an AI tool saves wait for you to press Get the page.
Updates install exactly the release that was published, never a look-alike.
Clips: trim the start, the end or parts in the middle of a recording.
Connect Claude, ChatGPT or Grok by signing in, with no token to copy.
Your stars, rail pins and recent items are now part of the nightly backup.
Every app shows the same message when something couldn't load, with Try again, and the same empty screen.
Share links are made only from Share, and AI tools must read a file's latest version before changing it.
Links remembers where you stopped reading and shows how much you've read.
Settings → Usage shows admins which apps the team uses, week by week.
Settings is a few small pages (General, Connections, Apps, and Organization for admins) instead of one long scroll.
Settings is grouped by topic, and Run setup again walks through every setup step without signing you out.
One click on the Chrome extension saves the page you're on to Links.
Pin as many apps to the rail as you like.
While you dictate, a warm glow hugs the edges of the window you're typing into.
Links keeps a copy of the page as you saw it when you save it from Chrome.
